Zodra de gezamenlijke maximale waarde van € 8.620.000 exclusief btw is bereikt, eindigen de overeenkomsten van rechtswege en worden geen nadere opdrachten meer verstrekt, ook niet als de maximale looptijd nog niet is verstreken. title: Greece – Transport agency services – Παροχή υπηρεσιών μεταφοράς έργων τέχνης της έκθεσης με θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας»
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η παροχή υπηρεσιών μεταφορών έργων τέχνης και ειδικότερα συσκευασία, μεταφορά και ανάρτηση έργων της περιοδικής έκθεσης με θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας». Αναλυτικότερα, οι υπηρεσίες παρέχονται σε δύο (2) φάσεις: Φάση Α1. Εγκατάσταση της περιοδικής έκθεση με θέμα: «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας» στο χώρο των περιοδικών εκθέσεων, στο επίπεδο -2 του κεντρικού κτιρίου της ΕΠΜΑΣ που βρίσκεται στο επίπεδο -2 του Α΄κτιρίου Η εγκατάσταση θα υλοποιηθεί τους μήνες Νοέμβριο – Δεκέμβριο 2026. Περιλαμβάνονται ενέργειες συντονισμού παραλαβής έργων τέχνης από φυσικά ή νομικά πρόσωπα που δανείζουν τα έργα τους στην αναθέτουσα αρχή, συσκευασίας, παραλαβής, μεταφοράς και ανάρτησης/ εγκατάστασης έργων τέχνης εντός και εκτός του νομού Αττικής και εκτός Ελλάδος μετακίνησης έργων τέχνης μεταξύ των εγκαταστάσεων της αναθέτουσας αρχής στην Αττική, μεταφοράς έργων τέχνης από παράρτημα της αναθέτουσας αρχής εκτός του νομού Αττικής, όπως και τοποθέτησης ή μετακίνησης υάλινων προπετασμάτων προθηκών καθώς και μετακίνησης προθηκών ή αντικειμένων που σχετίζονται με την έκθεση. Φάση Α2. Απεγκατάσταση της περιοδικής έκθεσης με Θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρας» από χώρο των περιοδικών εκθέσεων στο κτίριο της Εθνικής Πινακοθήκης – Μουσείο Αλεξάνδρου Σούτσου . Περιλαμβάνονται ενέργειες, συντονισμού παράδοσης έργων τέχνης, αποανάρτησης/ απεγκατάστασης συσκευασίας και μεταφοράς/ παράδοσης έργων τέχνης στα φυσικά ή νομικά πρόσωπα (εντός και εκτός Αττικής και εκτός Ελλάδος), που έχουν δανείσει έργα τους για να συμμετάσχουν στην έκθεση με θέμα «Νικηφόρος Λύτρα», καθώς και α) εσωτερικές μεταφορές έργων τέχνης των συλλογών της αναθέτουσας αρχής εντός του κτιριακού συγκροτήματος που διεξάγεται η έκθεση, β) μεταφορές στις εγκαταστάσεις της αναθέτουσας αρχής στην Αττική, γ) μεταφορές έργων τέχνης σε παράρτημα της Αναθέτουσας Αρχής εκτός του νομού Αττικης (Σπάρτη), καθώς και γ) εκ νέου ανάρτηση έργων τέχνης στους χώρους των μονίμων συλλογών της αναθέτουσας αρχής. Η απεγκατάσταση θα υλοποιηθεί τον Οκτώβριο του 2027.

title: Government-Owned Contractor Operated (GOCO) Aircraft/Ground Fuel Services and Fuel Storage and Distribution at Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ and Luke AFB, AZ
description: Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) Energy is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Alongside Aircraft Refueling Services to include managing, maintaining, and operating Government Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) facilities and equipment at Cannon, AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. The Contractor will ensure safe, accurate, and timely handling, quality control, and accountability of all Defense Wide Working Capital Fund (DWWCF)-owned petroleum products under their control. The Contractor will perform required maintenance to ensure facilities, associated systems, vehicles, and equipment remain operational to meet the base mission. The Contractor will comply with environmental protection, safety, and security directives. The Contractor will conduct required training to ensure personnel are fully qualified to perform Performance Work Statement (PWS) tasks. The Contractor shall conduct all necessary fuels operations to support base operations, airshows and special events, deployments, exercises, and contingencies under normal conditions, as well as, during periods of heightened security, inclement weather, or other unique situations. Operations must be safely and efficiently conducted to receive, store, transfer, issue, and account for products with appropriate controls to ensure fuel quality, maintain inventory accuracy, and ensure no environmental impact. The Contractor shall operate and maintain the self-service automated service station facilities, equipment, and systems and ensure sufficient product is available to provide 24 hours a day, seven days a week support of ground fuels. The Contractor shall perform required tasks to ensure fuel is properly accounted for and issued to only authorized users. This procurement will be 100% set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Business (SDVOSB) under NAICS code 493190 (Other Warehouse and Storage). The Government anticipates issuing one solicitation and awarding four (4) firm fixed-price contracts for Cannon AFB, NM, Holloman AFB, NM, Davis Monthan AFB, AZ, and Luke AFB, AZ. These requirements will be for a four-year base period (December 01, 2026 � November 30, 2030), a five-year option period (December 01, 2030 � November 30, 2035), and a option to extend the contract s for up to six individual months (December 01, 2035 � May 31, 2036).This procurement will be solicited under full and open competition after exclusion of sources. The solicitation will be published electronically on the SAM website at https://sam.gov/. Interested companies responding to the solicitation will be required to register in the System for Award Management (SAM) and Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). Dates of the Pre-Preproposal conference, in conjunction with the site visits, will be listed in the solicitation or via amendment. Offerors will be required to submit in writing to the Contract Specialist (via e-mail) the name(s) of the individual(s) who plan to attend.

title: Performance Assurance Services
description: The Marine Corps Logistics Command intends to award a sole-source contract to Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, for Performance Assurance, preventive maintenance, inspection, testing, and related maintenance support services for Government-owned industrial manufacturing equipment located at Production Plant Barstow, Yermo Annex, Yermo, California. Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, is the only authorized source capable of providing Performance Assurance services for the Haas and OMAX equipment covered by this requirement. The Government�s current intent is to include additional equipment manufactured by companies other than Haas and OMAX under the same contract for contract-administration convenience, coordinated scheduling, continuity of service, centralized accountability, and mitigation of performance and operational risks. The anticipated scope includes scheduled Performance Assurance services, preventive maintenance, equipment inspections, functional assessments, calibration analysis, vibration analysis, geometry inspections, Renishaw ballbar testing, drawbar force testing, OMAX annual waterjet services, replacement of specifically included maintenance components, equipment-condition reporting, and recommendations for follow-on corrective maintenance or spare parts. The requirement covers Government-owned industrial machines manufactured by Haas, OMAX, LVD/Strippit, Cincinnati, Fadal, Trumpf, Hyundai-Kia Machine, and Hardinge. The anticipated contract will include a base period and option periods. The Government does not intend to issue or post a solicitation for the Haas and OMAX portion of this requirement because Phillips Corporation, Federal Division, is the only authorized source for the required Performance Assurance services. However, before making a final acquisition determination, the Government is conducting market research to determine whether qualified sources exist to service the covered equipment manufactured by companies other than Haas and OMAX and whether separating that portion of the requirement would be in the Government�s best interest. This notice is not a request for quotations or proposals. Responsible sources may submit capability statements addressing only their ability to provide Performance Assurance services for the covered equipment manufactured by companies other than Haas and OMAX. Responses concerning the Haas and OMAX equipment are not requested. Capability statements must clearly demonstrate the firm�s ability to: Service the applicable equipment manufactured by LVD/Strippit, Cincinnati, Fadal, Trumpf, Hyundai-Kia Machine, and Hardinge; Identify the specific manufacturers, equipment models, and services the firm is capable of supporting; Provide qualified personnel with applicable OEM training, certifications, authorizations, or demonstrated experience; Perform the required preventive maintenance, inspections, functional testing, condition assessments, and reporting; Provide all required labor, supervision, tools, diagnostic equipment, travel, maintenance components, and technical expertise; and Meet applicable OEM requirements, manufacturer-recommended maintenance practices, and technician qualification requirements. Interested sources must submit their capability statements electronically to GySgt Matthew Radi at matthew.radi@usmc.mil no later than 25 September 2026 at 9:00 am EDT Submissions must include, at a minimum: Company name and address; Unique Entity Identifier and CAGE Code; Business size and applicable socioeconomic status; Point of contact information; Specific manufacturers and equipment models the firm can service; Applicable OEM authorizations, certifications, or technician qualifications; Relevant experience performing similar services; and Sufficient technical information for the Government to evaluate the firm�s capability. The Government will use the information received solely for acquisition-planning and market-research purposes, including determining whether it is in the Government�s best interest to separate the non-Haas and non-OMAX equipment from the contemplated Phillips sole-source contract. If the Government determines that separating the requirement is not practicable or in its best interest, it may proceed with an integrated sole-source award to Phillips Corporation, Federal Division. A determination regarding whether to separate any portion of the requirement is solely within the Government�s discretion. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs associated with preparing or submitting a capability statement. The Government is not obligated to acknowledge responses, conduct discussions, or award a contract as a result of this notice.

title: IRB Digital Case Management TBIPS
description: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) requires professional services support to the Chief Innovation and Technology Office (CITO) to advance the modernization of the IRB’s current case management application ecosystem through the Digital Case Modernization (DCM) initiative. This support will enable the IRB to define, design, validate, and implement modern digital solutions that improve the sustainability, interoperability, security, and scalability of its case management capabilities. The DCM initiative is intended to address current limitations in the IRB case management environment. Through this requirement, the IRB seeks specialized expertise to support analysis, architecture, technical design, software development, integration, testing, documentation, and knowledge transfer activities required to modernize the platform in a controlled and phased manner. More specifically, the objective is to support the transition of the IRB case management ecosystem toward a modernized, cloud-aligned microservices architecture and operating model that can better support future service improvements, business agility, data sharing, reporting, and the introduction of emerging capabilities such as advanced automation and Artificial Intelligence.

description: The National Research Council Canada (NRC), through the Central Facilities team at the Propulsion and Power Laboratory (PROPEL), has a requirement for the engineering, design, supply, and commissioning support of two Class 900, 10-inch full-bore ball valves designed for high-temperature service up to 1500°F High-Pressure Air Distribution isolation valves. description: 1. Scope 1.1. Purpose The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) requires contracted support for the set up of our new office spaces at the Joe Tobie Building in Yellowknife 2nd and 3rd floor 1.2. This designated POC is the CAF TA (Technical Authority), or representative, for whom the work is being carried out. The TA is responsible for all matters concerning the technical requirements of the work. 4. Deliverables 4.1. The Contractor must provide the services detailed in Section 3 of this Statement of Work. All item locations will be outlined prior to install for which room they all go into. • 10x U- shaped Height Adjustable desk with a file storage pedestal approx. 72W x 96D x 48H • 4 x Bookcase approx. 30W x 12D x 65H • 7x Flip top tables approx. 60W x 24D x 29H • 1x L-Shaped reception desk approx. 72W x 72D x 47H • 19x Mesh back chair with tilt function • 22x Black coat rack • 3x Square coffee table approx. 36W x 36D x 22H • 2x Leather or fabric lounge chair approx. 30W x 33D x 31H • 28x 2 drawer file cabinet on wheels • 14x L-Shaped height adjustable desk approx. 72W x 72D x 48H • 16x Mesh high back-office chair • 3x Square seated height table approx. 36W x 36D x 29H • 17x Mesh back guest chair • 3x Height adjustable desk approx. 70W x 23D x 48H • 36x Mesh high back chair with tilt function • 3x Black leather high back executive office chair • 2x Boardroom table approx. 96W x 48D x 29H • 4x Leather or fabric guest chair • 7x Height adjustable desk approx. 58W x 23D x 48H • 3x flip top table approx. 72W x 24D x 29H questions 1. Solicitation / delivery timeline: The solicitation requires all deliverables to be received on or before October 10, 2026. Could you please confirm the anticipated contract award date and whether the October 10 delivery and installation deadline remains firm? Unfortunately yes the deadline is firm 2. U-shaped height-adjustable desks – Line 1: Could you confirm whether the entire U-shaped workstation is required to be height adjustable, or whether a height-adjustable main desk with fixed return/back credenza would be acceptable, provided the overall workstation meets the required form, dimensions and functionality? Yes that is acceptable 3. Desk orientation: For Line 1 (U-shaped HA desk), Line 4 (L-shaped reception desk), and Line 10 (L-shaped HA desk), are specific left/right bridge or return orientations required? Appendix 1 does not appear to identify the furniture orientation. Would reversible configurations be acceptable, or will the required orientation be confirmed with the Technical Authority prior to installation? The orientation will be confirmed with the Technical Authority at contract award 4. Furniture finishes: Other than the colors specifically identified in the SOW, are there any required finishes, laminate types, colors or branding standards for the furniture? In particular, is HPL required, or may standard commercial laminate finishes be proposed? Besides the finishes listed for the items in the SOW the remaining finishes can be HPL or Standard laminate as long as they are all the same color. 5. Existing room finishes: Are any photographs, finish schedules, or proposed paint/flooring selections available for the 2nd and 3rd floor spaces? If not, may the Offeror propose standard neutral furniture finishes for items where no finish is specified? Yes the offeror can propose furniture finishes. At the moment there is no furniture in the building and walls are just white.

description: VOORAANKONDIGING EUROPESE OPENBARE AANBESTEDING Dit betreft een vooraankondiging waarmee de gemeente Rotterdam de markt vroegtijdig wil informeren over een aankomende opdracht, nog vóórdat de eigenlijke aanbestedingsprocedure formeel van start gaat, zodat geinteresserde ondernemers zich kunnen voorbereiden. Bij een vooraankondiging kunnen partijen zich nog niet aanmelden, nog niet inschrijven, nog geen vragen stellen of formele aanbestedingsdocumentatie inzien. De werkelijke inschrijving kan pas zodra de officiële aanbesteding wordt gepubliceerd. De Bosdreef wordt in twee fasen naar het noorden verlegd om ruimte te maken voor de nieuwe woonwijk Nieuw Kralingen en een bedrijvenstrook. Fase 1 is opgeleverd in 2024. Op of omstreeks 19 juni 2026 wordt de Europese openbare aanbesteding gepubliceerd voor de opgave van fase 2. Het doel van de Opdracht van fase 2 is de realisatie van fase 2 van de Verlegde Bosdreef als volwaardige noordelijke ontsluitingsroute (1x2-baansweg, 50 km/u) ter vervanging van de huidige Bosdreef (thans 2x2-baansweg, 70 km/u). De beoogde startdatum van de werkzaamheden in deze Opdracht fase 2 staat gepland op 1 februari 2027. De Opdracht die in de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure zal worden beschreven gaat over: Nieuw wegtracé (50 km/u-gebiedsontsluitingsweg) met fundering, verharding, markering en wegmeubilair Compleet rioleringssysteem (hemel- en vuilwater) aansluitend op bestaande infrastructuur Operationele VRI's en openbare verlichting Nieuwe, bredere betonnen Crooswijksebrug (niet-beweegbaar) Geïntegreerd infrastructuursysteem Volledige verbinding tussen fase 1 en fase 2 Vergunningen, keuringen, opleverdocumentatie en overdracht aan beheer (RAW-systematiek) Het werk bestaat in hoofdzaak uit : Grondwerk (ontgraven en ophogen inclusief verwerken) Het slopen van een betonnen brug (inclusief fundatie) Het bouwen van een betonnen brug (inclusief fundatie) Het aanbrengen van en grondkering (stalen damwand met verankering) Verwijderen asfaltverharding Aanbrengen asfaltverharding inclusief fundering Aanbrengen elementenverharding inclusief fundering Aanbrengen / installeren van een gemaal Aanleg DIT-riolering / riolering Aanleg persleiding Aanleg waterberging Aanleg verkeersregelinstallaties Aanleg installatie openbare verlichting Bijkomende werkzaamheden De bovenstaande opsomming van werkzaamheden is slechts een indicatie van de te verrichten werkzaamheden en alleen bedoeld om de interesse van potentiële Inschrijvers voor de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure te wekken. Inschrijvers kunnen geen rechten ontlenen aan deze opsomming. Zie voor een nadere technische omschrijving van de uit te voeren werkzaamheden de aanbestedingsleidraad en het daarbij gevoegde RAW-bestek zoals dat op of omstreeks 19 juni 2026 zal worden gepubliceerd via dit Aanbestedingsplatform.

title: Netherlands – Medical software development services – Digitaal Dossier Jeugdgezondheidszorg
description: De aanbestedende dienst doorloopt een Europese aanbestedingsprocedure om een robuust en toekomstbestendig DDJGZ te selecteren en implementeren. Het systeem moet volledig operationeel en gebruiksklaar worden opgeleverd. Het DDJGZ moet voldoen aan de gestelde functionele en technische eisen en duurzaam zijn ingericht. De gekozen SaaS-oplossing moet een schaalbare basis bieden voor verdere ontwikkeling en toekomstige behoeften binnen de Jeugdgezondheidszorg. De opdracht betreft de levering, implementatie en het beheer van een SaaS‑applicatie (DDJGZ) ten behoeve van de Jeugdgezondheidszorg. De scope omvat configuratie, datamigratie, koppelingen met relevante externe systemen, opleiding van gebruikers en doorlopend beheer en support. Het systeem moet beschikbaar zijn voor circa 230 medewerkers en geschikt zijn voor opschaling. De overeenkomst heeft een looptijd van 10 jaar inclusief optionele verlengingen.

title: France – Site preparation work – Réalisation des travaux préparatoires à l’extension d’une installation nucléaire existante
description: Le CEA projette la construction d’un bâtiment d’extension d’une installation existante sur le centre de Valduc. Afin de garantir la parfaite préparation de l’emplacement retenu, le CEA souhaite, à travers le marché objet de ce présent avis, réaliser les travaux préparatoires nécessaires à l’aménagement de la zone de construction. Ces travaux correspondent aux prestations suivantes : - L’aménagement de la zone de chantier ; - La dépose et le dévoiement de réseaux existants sur la zone ; - Le réaménagement du merlon situé sur le bâtiment adjacent au futur bâtiment, y compris la dépose d’ouvrages existants ; - La réalisation de la plateforme du futur bâtiment et des futures bases vies pour la phase travaux ; - L’évacuation sur le site des matériaux de déblais excédentaires ; - L’amenée de tous les réseaux nécessaires (dont Eaux Usées, Eaux Industriels, Eau Potable, Infrastructures pour Courants Forts et Courants Faibles Industriels). Les travaux du présent Marché correspondent aux travaux préparatoires préalables à la construction d’une extension d’un Bâtiment existant. Ces travaux comprennent en part ferme : • La zone d’installation chantier du Titulaire, y compris signalisation de chantier, • La réalisation des éléments assurant la délimitation de la future zone chantier qui comprend : o L’implantation des limitations des futurs ouvrages o La mise en place de clôtures et de barrières de protection o La réalisation de la plateforme et des sujétions associées au futur poste de gardiennage, y compris réseaux secs et humides • La dépose et/ou dévoiement de réseaux secs et humides (dont EP, EI, AEP, CFO, CFI,) • Le réaménagement du merlon du bâtiment existant avec les sujétions associées dont notamment : o La dépose du merlon (environ 7500m3) o La dépose d’ouvrages d’existants en béton armé (ouvrages de soutènement et galerie extérieure) o La réalisation de nouveaux ouvrages de soutènement en béton armé pour le merlon en toiture sur 50ml environ o La mise en bardage du voile extérieur du bâtiment existant, y compris toutes sujétions (60m x 12m environ) • L’aménagement de la plateforme de la future extension (environ 1500 m3 de déblai) (profondeur d’environ 1m) • L’aménagement de la zone des bases vie pour une surface approximative de 1300m² • L’évacuation des matériaux de déblai (zone de dépose sur le site à 1.5 km en aller simple) • La mise en place des réseaux, postes et équipements électriques pour le futur chantier depuis le bâtiment existant (1 armoire de distribution générale de chantier alimentant les bases vie, les grues et les coffrets de chantier) • La mise en place des arrivées de réseaux secs et humides pour les futures bases vies de chantier • La dépose et l’évacuation du poste électrique HT/BT existant et présent sur l’emprise chantier ainsi que les structures associées, y compris liaisons électriques • Un suivi géotechnique de type mission G3 • La pose de candélabres sur poteau bois avec haut-parleurs (environ une dizaine) • L’établissement de tous les documents nécessaires à la bonne exécution des travaux (études d’exécution, documents d’organisation de chantier...) mentionnés supra • La réalisation des contrôles et essais à réaliser pour les postes mentionnés supra • Le dossier des ouvrages exécutés Les prestations optionnelles à réaliser au titre du marché sont décrites infra. Les prestations prévues au BPU vont notamment concerner les domaines suivants : • Le détour d’un camion de terre de déblais par l’entrée du centre de Valduc pour contrôle radiologique (distance 6km en aller simple) • L’évacuation sur le site des matériaux de déblais excédentaires • Un arrêt de chantier d’un jour • Un arrêt de chantier d’une semaine ouvrée NOTA 1 : cette liste de prestations prévues au BPU n’est pas exhaustive. NOTA 2 : Les volumes précisés supra correspondent à des quantités estimées par le CEA. Elles ne constituent pas un engagement du CEA. Les prestations optionnelles du marché sont les suivantes : • L’agrandissement du bassin d’orage (130m3 maximum) • Alimentation des bases vie depuis un futur poste HT BT (hors périmètre de ce marché) (environ 200ml) Les prestations se déroulent sur le Centre CEA/DAM de VALDUC en Zone Protégée avec contraintes d’accès et d’exploitation.

title: Medicaid Enterprise Systems (MES) IT Standards - Request for Information (RFI)
description: CMS seeks feedback from all Medicaid Enterprise System (MES) stakeholders to inform the development and implementation of the MES IT Standards Program. We invite input from State Medicaid Agencies, MES technology vendors, systems integrators, Standards Development Organizations (SDOs), healthcare providers, and other industry experts. The goal of this RFI is to gather specific, actionable information to ensure the program effectively addresses the most significant barriers to MES transformation. We seek to understand which elements of the current ecosystem are working well, which require improvement, and how CMS can best support states and vendors in transitioning to a more standardized, interoperable, and cost-effective future. To aid in our understanding of the submitted responses, please be clear and concise and preface your responses with the corresponding question label (e.g., SA-1, V-2). The RFI will be open for 45 days from the date of posting. Please submit responses via email to the listed Points of Contact.

Work includes demolition and removal of existing pumps, grinder, auger, electrical disconnects, transfer switch, and controls; installation of new lift station equipment; electrical upgrades; controls modernization; testing; commissioning; and staff training. All work must maintain continuous sewage system operation and comply with Federal, State, Local, NEC, NFPA 820, OSHA, and FBOP security requirements. Place of Performance: Federal Correctional Institution Cumberland 14601 Burbridge Rd. SE Cumberland, MD 21502 Scope of Work Includes: (See attached Statement of Work) � Removal and disposal of existing lift station equipment. � Installation of new stainless?steel NEMA 4X control panel with PLC/relay logic, VFDs, starters, surge protection, HOA switches. � New level?sensing system with redundancy and audio/visual alarms. � Installation of new grinder, auger, diverters, three wet?well pumps, and three spare pumps. � Replacement of incoming disconnects, automatic transfer switch, and associated wiring. � Upgraded grounding, conduits, surge/lightning protection, and fail?safe logic. � Full functional testing, hydrostatic testing, manufacturer startup, and calibration. � Minimum 6 hours of on?site training and provision of all as?built documentation, O&M manuals, warranties, schematics, and PLC programming. Evaluation Factors: Award will be made on best value. Price, past performance, and specifications will be evaluated. Quotes are due September 25, 2026. 10 AM (EST) Please email quotes to Brian Logsdon at blogsdon@bop.gov using the provided SF1449 (15B10727Q00000015) Please provide UEI, email, company name, complete box 30A, 30B, and 30C, total aggregate price, and total calendar days for project completion.

buyer: HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, DEPARTMENT OF
title: Medicaid Enterprise Systems (MES) IT Standards - Request for Information (RFI)
description: CMS seeks feedback from all Medicaid Enterprise System (MES) stakeholders to inform the development and implementation of the MES IT Standards Program. We invite input from State Medicaid Agencies, MES technology vendors, systems integrators, Standards Development Organizations (SDOs), healthcare providers, and other industry experts. The goal of this RFI is to gather specific, actionable information to ensure the program effectively addresses the most significant barriers to MES transformation. We seek to understand which elements of the current ecosystem are working well, which require improvement, and how CMS can best support states and vendors in transitioning to a more standardized, interoperable, and cost-effective future. To aid in our understanding of the submitted responses, please be clear and concise and preface your responses with the corresponding question label (e.g., SA-1, V-2). The RFI will be open for 45 days from the date of posting. Please submit responses via email to MACBIS-Enterprise-Services@cms.hhs.gov and aaron.blackshire@cms.hhs.gov.

title: Market Intelligence Notice: Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station Taxiway A4 & Runway Extension Project - Use of Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE Place of Performance: Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station (NFARS), New York Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 237310 � Highway, Street and Bridge Construction. (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction to extend Runway 10-28 and associated taxiways at the Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station, New York. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver fully functional airfield improvements. The primary project elements include: a. Reconstructing the existing overrun/blast pad on Runway 28 end to full-strength airfield pavement. b. Extending Runway 10-28 and extending Taxiway A4 to connect the 914th ARW apron to the new Runway 28 end. c. Extending a 520-foot portion of Runway 6-24 and providing a warmup pad for two (2) KC-135R aircraft. The potential total area of new airfield pavement is approximately 780,000 sq ft. d. Modifying the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Medium-Intensity Approach Lighting System with Runway End Identification Lights (MALSR) approach lighting, which requires active coordination with FAA construction representatives during removal and re-installation. e. Installing new airfield electrical and lighting systems, including runway edge lights, runway centerline lights, threshold lights, touchdown zone lights, airfield signage, and taxiway edge lights. f. Constructing a new creek culvert to allow the new taxiway to traverse the Cayuga Creek. g. Erecting a jet blast deflector fence on the Runway 28 end. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $50,000,000.00 CRITICAL PROJECT CONSTRAINTS & CHALLENGES: Geotechnical Constraints: The project site features variable and shallow bedrock (as shallow as 3 feet below grade) and a high groundwater table that heavily complicates subdrainage and stormwater design. Sensitive Environmental Conditions: Work will occur near federal and state-regulated wetlands and Cayuga Creek. The site is a habitat for the Devil Crayfish, which is listed as a species of Greatest Conservation Needs. Multiple permits with State and Federal agencies will be required prior to construction. Operational Constraints: A significant portion of the work will occur within the active runway Controlled Movement Area (CMA). Work requires compliance with an FAA-approved Construction Safety and Phasing Plan (CSPP), temporary displaced threshold markings, modifications to NAVAIDS, and FAA flight checks. Security Constraints: Strict security constraints are in place, requiring Government escorts at all times during construction. Airfield Pavement Quality Control: Onsite batch plant space (approx. 6 acres) has been identified. Review and final approval of concrete and asphalt mix designs reside with the USACE Transportation Service Center (TSC). The TSC will provide a mandatory, weeklong airfield pavement workshop prior to the start of construction, which the contractor�s key personnel must attend. Stakeholder Coordination: The contract requires active coordination with the airport operator (Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority - NFTA), USACE, Air Force Reserve Command (AFRC), FAA, and Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station (NFARS). PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGIES UNDER EVALUATION: Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. Currently, the Government has advanced the design to 35% and has the capability to progress to a full design. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The CM@Risk Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This Course of Action utilizes the 10 U.S.C. � 2808a OT authority to execute a construction project where the design is at 35% completion. Phase 1 Preconstruction: The builder is hired during Phase 1 to act as an expert consultant, helping the Designer of Record (DOR) push the design from 35% to 100% using real-time market data and MII (MCACES 2nd Generation) cost comparisons. Phase 2 Construction: Once the design hits 100% and the MII estimate validates the open-book pricing, the agreement transitions to Phase 2, where the builder goes "At-Risk" to construct the facility under a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). The DOR retains design liability, but the contractor drives constructability and assumes responsibility for layout, schedule, and trade coordination. The CM@Risk Pricing Structure: Preconstruction Services Fee: A small, fixed-price or time-and-materials amount paid to the contractor strictly to fund their time spent helping the Architect Engineer (A/E) finalize the 35% design into a 100% design. The Target Fee: The contractor�s transparent profit margin for managing the actual construction, bid competitively upfront. The GMP: The absolute ceiling for the construction phase (Validated Direct Costs + Target Fee + Shared Contingency). PHASED EXECUTION PLAN Phase 1: Preconstruction Services Agreement (CM@Risk Advisory) Solicitation (White Papers): The Solicitation would likely include the 35% design. The Deliverable is anticipated to be a concise 5-10 page White Paper. Evaluation Criteria will likely include Corporate capability and experience with collaborative project delivery methods ( including CM@Risk, Progressive Design-Build (PDB) and/or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB)) under an OT framework; preconstruction approach (how the firm plans to collaborate with the Government's A/E to close the remaining 65% design gap, identify value-engineering opportunities, and mitigate supply-chain risks); proposed Target Fee (for construction) and Preconstruction Services Fee. The Pitch Meeting (Oral Presentations): A 90-minute pitch where the contractor must bring their Project Manager, Site Superintendent, and their Preconstruction Manager. The Government team assesses how well the contractor's team will integrate with the A/E during the critical final design push. The OT is initially awarded and funded only for the Preconstruction Services Fee. Design Finalization (Bridging the 65% Gap): The contractor�s Preconstruction team sits with the Government and the DOR. Because the design is not locked, they can actively change it. They perform value engineering, finalize equipment selections, and ensure the drawings are 100% constructible. buyer: European Union, represented by the European Commission on behalf of and for the account of Guatemala
title: Guatemala – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Asistencia Técnica para la implementación de la Agenda de inversiones Global Gateway en Guatemala – Global Gateway Facility Guatemala
description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. La Asistencia Técnica contribuirá a: mejorar la alineación, coordinación y monitoreo de las iniciativas implementadas en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway en Guatemala; promover un marco regulatorio e institucional que favorezca la inversión sostenible en los sectores prioritarios de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway; impulsar proyectos de inversión sostenibles, transformadores y sensibles a la igualdad de género y a las buenas prácticas internacionales en materia de derechos y protección del medioambiente en los sectores prioritarios y a posicionar los intereses del sector privado europeo en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway para Guatemala. Sin excluir otras potenciales áreas de trabajo prioritarias para la UE y Guatemala, y reconociendo la flexibilidad dinámica de la estrategia Global Gateway, las áreas prioritarias para Guatemala actualmente incluyen transición verde (transporte sostenible, energía renovable e integración eléctrica regional, economía circular, gestión sostenible de recursos naturales y residuos) y transición digital (conectividad, gobernanza digital, ciberseguridad, innovación digital, observación de la Tierra, inteligencia artificial).

eContent Books RFI
description: The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a Cabinet-level executive branch department of the Federal Government whose workforce is comprised of approximately 650,000 clinical and non-clinical personnel (of which approximately 450,000 are employees) charged with providing lifelong healthcare services to eligible military veterans at the 1,380 health care facilities, including 170 VA medical centers and 1,193 outpatient sites located throughout the country. Non-healthcare benefits include disability compensation, vocational rehabilitation, education assistance, home loans, and life insurance. The VA also provides burial and memorial benefits to eligible veterans and family members at the 157 VA managed or 125 VA grant-funded cemeteries. VA employs a highly skilled and multi-faceted workforce aligned with its mission, program, and operational needs. Workforce Development is one of the key factors to recruiting and retaining a high-performing workforce. VA employs individuals at every competency and skill level whether they are new to the workforce or experts in their occupation. That said, VA workforce needs differ at every career stage. VA Federal personnel are encouraged annually to complete My Development Plans (MDP). They work with supervisors to determine short and long- term career goals as well as short-term training needs. Training needs are then documented on the MDP. The VA�s Leadership Development Framework (LDF) is based on the Federal-wide United States Office of Personnel Management Executive Core Qualifications. By using the VA LDF, VA personnel will be better able to assess their leadership capabilities for developmental purposes and to support the Department�s workforce, talent development, and succession planning efforts. Certain VA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices require its workforce to complete technical competency assessments and leadership competency assessments for non-supervisory positions. VA personnel will complete leadership and technical competency assessments through the Department�s Talent Management System (TMS) 2.0 or Learning Management system of record (LMS). VA personnel must also meet certain training requirements throughout the year. These requirements may be prescribed as Federal Mandatory Training such as No Fear Act, Information Security Awareness, Occupational Health, and Safety, or Telework. Some personnel must complete training required by their occupation or role such as Cyber security role-based training. VA personnel access most of their training through Talent Management System TMS 2.0. This platform provides a common LMS and learning content services that enable VA to maximize the return on taxpayer investment. TMS 2.0 has a robust and secure environment to accommodate approximately 450,000 end users, ~12,000 administrators and over 500 unique domains. TMS 2.0 is the Department-wide system for managing training records and activities at VA. The purpose of this contract is to acquire eContent, Digital Books, Professional Development Training and Support Services to meet the training requirement of VA.

description: IDA Ireland is seeking to establish of a Single Party Framework for the Design, Delivery and Management of IDA Ireland’s Property Management System on the Salesforce platform. Justification for the maximum 7 years Framework length - The successful candidate may be required to undertake potentially significant upfront time investment in further discovery, detailed solution design, data migration, configuration, testing, integration and organisational change activities. In its current off-the-shelf form, a Salesforce solution is not capable of meeting all of IDA Property’s requirements without tailoring and multiple integration points with third party systems. This will be delivered through controlled configuration and integration activities that will may require extended timescales. The option of the extension of the framework to a maximum of 7 years will allow the IDA (provided that the successful tenderer has performed in a satisfactory manner) to obtain the benefit of the framework support as envisaged in the event of a prolonged implementation period.

title: Brand Name Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS)
description: 8 September 2026 Update Solicitation/Draft contract change in Statement of Work Combined Synopsis/Solicitation: Brand Name Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) Solicitation Number: FA8601-26-Q-0074 Notice Type: Special Notice (RFQ) Issuing Office: AFLCMC/PZIBA Posted Date: 9 September 2026 Response Date: 25 September 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT Set-Aside: N/A Product Service Code: 6630 NAICS Code: 334516 Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 Employees Description The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA), on behalf of the Department of the Air Force at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, intends to award a Brand Name Only, firm-fixed-price contract for an Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS). This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the RFO, effective 17 April 2026, and the Revolutionary Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (RDFARS) as of the date of issuance. The Department of the Air Force intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for an Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW), dated 1 September 2026, on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable basis. The Schedule of Supplies, place of performance, delivery information, and the full list of applicable provisions and clauses are set forth in the attached SF 1449 and solicitation. Award is subject to the availability of funds. The requirement is for all supplies, labor, and services necessary to procure a new High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS). This is a follow-on acquisition requiring the new HPLC-MS to be fully compatible and interchangeable with the agency�s existing Agilent equipment and software. The Government�s market research indicates that Agilent products use proprietary MassHunter software for instrument control and data analysis, and no other manufacturer produces a compatible system that meets the Government�s essential need for a single, integrated platform while avoiding the cost of new training and method redevelopment. The approved Brand Name Justification is attached to this posting. Submission Instructions Submission Deadline: 25 September 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT Required Email Subject Line: FA8601-26-Q-0074, Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) Offerors shall submit proposals by email to all of the following points of contact: Candice Snow candice.snow@us.af.mil Alejandro Quiles alejandro.quiles_sanchez.1@us.af.mil Brian Algeo brian.algeo.1@us.af.mil Format: Submit a single email not exceeding 5 MB. Attachments must be in PDF, DOCX, or XLSX format. Compressed files, including ZIP files, are not permitted. Confirmation: A receipt confirmation will be sent within 24 hours. If confirmation is not received, contact all three points of contact listed above. Proposal Content Requirements Proposals shall consist of a Technical Proposal and a Price Proposal and shall provide sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance with the SOW. Offerors shall not merely restate Government requirements. Each proposal shall include: Company name, address, SAM Unique Entity ID, CAGE Code, and TIN. Point-of-contact name, telephone number, and email address. Proposal number, proposal date, and proposal validity period. Technical description, manuals, data sheets, or product literature demonstrating compliance with each SOW requirement. A complete price schedule matching the CLIN structure provided in the solicitation. Total Evaluated Price. Completed offeror representations and certifications, including country-of-origin information for the offered end product and applicable components. Itemized firm-fixed-price information with extended totals. Pricing shall include shipping, unloading, and final setup at AFIT Building 644, Room L139. Payment terms shall be Net 30. Progress payments are not authorized. Confirmation that the offeror is Agilent or an authorized Agilent reseller. If submitting an offer as an authorized reseller, the offeror shall provide a manufacturer authorization letter verifying authorization to sell the offered system to the Government. Technical description of the items offered sufficient to verify part-number accuracy and compliance with the SOW. Key Information Requirement: Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) in accordance with the SOW dated 1 September 2026. Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price. Period of Performance: Six months after contract award. Delivery: Delivery, installation, unloading, storage, and final setup shall occur at the Air Force Institute of Technology, Building 644, Room L139, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification In accordance with RDFARS 252.204-7021, this acquisition requires Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 1 for Federal Contract Information only. Offerors must have a current CMMC Level 1, or higher, self-assessment recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System at the time of award. Waivers, grace periods, and Plans of Action and Milestones are not permitted. Buy American Act and Qualifying-Country Products This acquisition is subject to the Buy American Act and the qualifying-country-product requirements set forth in the SOW. In accordance with the SOW, all products proposed or delivered shall be domestic end products or qualifying-country end products, as applicable. Offerors shall identify the country of origin for the offered end product and applicable components in the required representations and certifications. The offered HPLC-MS system must be made and assembled in the United States of America in accordance with the SOW. Basis for Award Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal: Conforms to this combined synopsis/solicitation; Receives an �Acceptable� rating for Technical Capability, as demonstrated by compliance with all SOW requirements, domestic assembly, and authorized Agilent sourcing credentials; and Contains the lowest Total Evaluated Price determined fair, reasonable, and not unbalanced. Past Performance and Responsibility Before award, the Contracting Officer will perform a responsibility determination under RFO Part 9, including review of the offeror�s record in the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System and the Supplier Performance Risk System. Adverse findings may render an offeror non-responsible. The Government reserves the right to award without discussions or to make no award. Important Notices SAM Registration: Offerors must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management for the life of the contract. Invoicing: Invoices shall be submitted electronically through Wide Area Workflow�Receipt and Acceptance. Payment shall be made as 100 percent Net 30 upon successful completion of all delivery, installation, and final setup requirements. Questions Questions shall be submitted by email to all three points of contact listed above no later than 16 September 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT. Include solicitation number FA8601-26-Q-0074 in the email subject line. Late questions may not be considered. title: Pakistan NDC 3.0 Delivery Coordination Mechanism (Federal-Provincial Coordination and Tracking)
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the Government of Pakistan. Pakistan has committed to reducing projected greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2035 through its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0. Delivering this target will depend heavily on action at the provincial level, where responsibility for many climate-relevant sectors rests. While the Government of Pakistan has established new coordination arrangements through the National Climate Finance Strategy (NCFS), challenges remain around federal-provincial coordination, implementation tracking, climate finance visibility, and reporting progress against national climate commitments. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance to support the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC), the Pakistan Climate Change Authority (PCCA), and provincial governments to establish and operationalise a practical federal-provincial coordination and tracking mechanism for NDC 3.0 implementation. The project will strengthen institutional coordination, improve monitoring and reporting of climate actions and investments, build government capacity, and support the mobilisation of climate finance. The intervention will also integrate Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) considerations to promote more inclusive climate governance and decision-making. Key outputs are expected to include a federal-provincial NDC coordination framework, a standardised NDC tracking and reporting framework, an interoperability pilot connecting existing government climate and public-sector data systems, operational support for a Tactical Climate Coordination Forum, and a sustainability and scale-up roadmap. The project aims to strengthen Pakistan's ability to implement and report on its climate commitments, improve evidence-based decision-making, enhance transparency and accountability, and create a stronger foundation for attracting climate finance and accelerating NDC delivery across provinces and sectors. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk.

title: Barracks Maintenance OTA
description: 1. INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) � Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. � 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. � 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. title: Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals in the following technical area: physics and nonlinear control of inertial measurement units (IMUs) appropriate for tactical and unmanned missions. The Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT) program will challenge the research community to overcome the decade-long performance plateau of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) IMUs by exploring revolutionary sensor architectures that operate in highly nonlinear regimes. DARPA is soliciting proposals for the research and development of novel inertial sensors based on physics such as, but not limited to, electromagnetically levitated proof masses, non-linear resonators, and high-velocity tethered microsystems. A central theme of this program is the tight co-design of the physical sensor package with advanced, real-time adaptive control systems necessary to stabilize and harness these complex dynamics. Performers should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.

title: Measurement of Benzene Emissions from Gasoline Dispensing Facilities
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)’s mandate includes the preservation and enhancement of the quality of the natural environment, including water, air and soil quality. Accordingly, ECCC works in conjunction with Health Canada (HC) and other departments to understand the risks posed by the release of toxic substances, then develop policy as needed to effectively manage these releases. Benzene is recognized as a human carcinogen by HC (Canada 1993) and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) (IARC 2018), among other international agencies. In addition, short-term exposure (over hours to days) is associated with hematotoxicity, including during fetal development. Benzene is a constituent of gasoline and, as a volatile organic compound (VOC), readily evaporates and is released into the atmosphere from gasoline service stations. Exposure to benzene through inhalation of emissions from these facilities may pose unacceptable risks to human health for members of the general population residing in the vicinity of gasoline stations. ECCC wishes to study benzene concentrations in the air in the vicinity of gasoline stations Canada, ideally in the Ottawa-Gatineau area, to improve understanding of the human health implications of benzene emissions from these facilities and validate the efficacy of emissions control equipment in cases where it is installed. The contractor will contribute to this objective by measuring ambient concentrations of benzene and, where feasible, other VOCs or total VOCs at gasoline stations before, during, and after gasoline deliveries, in accordance with the parameters set out in this Statement of Work. The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2027. For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

title: Flood Bank Realignment
description: This collaborative project with SBAG address recurring concerns over beaver burrowing and floodbank breaches on high-value farmland along the River Isla, a major tributary of the River Tay (SAC). By realigning a floodbank and creating a wider more natural river corridor with willow buffer strip we intend to increase bank resilience, reduce beaver impacts and enhance biodiversity. Two participating agricultural landowners will trial setback embankments and habitat features including beaver mounds to encourage coexistence. The approach integrates agricultural resilience with river naturalisation, monitored by the river Restoration Centre and Beaver Trust to inform future coexistence strategies to promote biodiversity.

By realigning a floodbank and creating a wider more natural river corridor with willow buffer strip we intend to increase bank resilience, reduce beaver impacts and enhance biodiversity. Two participating agricultural landowners will trial setback embankments and habitat features including beaver mounds to encourage coexistence. The approach integrates agricultural resilience with river naturalisation, monitored by the river Restoration Centre and Beaver Trust to inform future coexistence strategies to promote biodiversity.

buyer: The Common Services Agency (more commonly known as Public Services Delivery Scotland) (PSD Scotland)
title: Service Integration and Management System (SIAM)
description: PSD Scotland intends to procure a Service Integration and Management contract for the transition, stabilisation and continued delivery of selected national digital services supporting health and care across Scotland. The successful supplier will act as prime contractor and provide a single point of accountability for end-to-end service delivery, integration and performance. The supplier will also be responsible for the management of any subcontractors and dependencies with other providers and Authority teams. The initial priority will be to maintain continuity and stabilise these business-critical services as they transition away from the existing National IT Contract, while establishing a strong foundation for subsequent improvement and modernisation.

title: Program Manager Counterproliferation (PMCP) Service Support
description: **UPDATE AS OF 09 SEPTEMBER 2026** The purpose of this update is to notify industry that the final Request for Proposal (RFP) is scheduled for release the week of 21 September 2026, and that the Government has completed responses to all questions received during the Draft RFP phase. Due to Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) handling restrictions, the Q&A document will not be posted publicly and must be requested through formal access controls. To obtain access to the restricted Draft RFP Q&A document, interested parties must request access through SAM.gov. Prior to granting access, the government will verify that the contractor maintains a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment score of 110 posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). Once the Government confirms a vendor can receive and safeguard CUI, the Draft RFP Q&A document will be available for review in SAM.gov. Additionally, interested parties are hereby notified that the final RFP and all associated solicitation documentation will be issued, managed, and submitted exclusively through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. To facilitate timely access and ensure vendors are fully prepared to submit proposals, PIEE registration and user access instructions are attached to this notice. Vendors are strongly encouraged to verify account readiness and establish appropriate system roles in advance of the RFP release. Further, all interested vendors must submit a new executed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) to receive the final RFP. NDAs previously executed during the Draft RFP phase will not satisfy this requirement. The final RFP NDA is attached to this notice, and vendors are encouraged to execute and submit their NDAs in advance of the Government�s formal solicitation release scheduled for the week of 21 September. All signed NDAs shall be submitted via email to SOCOM.PMCP.SPTSVC.RFP.SHDMBX@socom.mil. The following link is provided to access the PIEE solicitation module training: https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/xhtml/wbt/sol/index.xhtml This notification includes three attachments: 1. PMCP-SS_RFP_NDA 2. PIEE_Solicitation_Module_Vendor_Access_Instructions 3. PMCPSS Draft RFP Q&A **UPDATE AS OF 25 AUGUST 2026** The purpose of this update is to notify industry that the final Request for Proposal (RFP) is scheduled for release on September 9, 2026. Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for H9240226RE003, Program Manager Counterproliferation (PMCP) Service Support Contract The Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology and Logistics (SOF AT&L) core mission is to provide rapid and focused acquisition, technology, and logistics support to SOF Warfighters. Under SOF AT&L, the Program Manager for Counterproliferation (PMCP) is chartered with the procurement, development, testing, training, fielding, and sustainment of technologies in support of Electronic Warfare (EW), advanced Counter Improvised Explosive Device (C-IED) operations and Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) for improvised explosive device threats and Counter-Unmanned System (C-UxS) threats. Interested industry partners are encouraged to submit a request, including company name and CAGE code to the below Points of Contact (POCs). This information will be used to verify in the System for Award management (SAM) and the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) that the offeror can receive CUI documents. After successful verification, the documents will be provided for review and submission of questions, comments, or suggestions. We are particularly interested in feedback regarding the clarity of evaluation criteria, pricing structure, and feasibility of the past performance relevancy measures. Please submit your feedback using the RFP Q&A Template provided with this RFP Letter to the POCs listed below no later than 1300 hours ET on 15 June 2026.

title: FSC Meridian Fire Reporting & Control Systems, NAS Meridian
description: Naval Air Station Meridian is located in east-central Mississippi, near Meridian, Mississippi in Lauderdale and Kemper counties. Approximately 20 miles northeast of the city of Meridian between State Highways 39 and 45. NAS Meridian hosts Training Air Wing One (TRAWING-1). The installation serves as a premier jet flight-training base, supporting Training Squadron 7 (VT-7) and Training Squadron 9 (VT-9). The air station trains hundreds of Navy and Marine Corps student aviators utilizing the T-45C Goshawk jet trainer. There are outlying fields used for student training. All maintenance and repair shall be performed by personnel trained and certified by the OEM. Personnel inspecting, witnessing tests, preparing reports, and issuing certificates for boilers and UPVs must be qualified per UFC 3-430-07. Personnel inspecting, certifying, and making recommendations for corrective action for backflow preventers shall be certified per UG-2029-ENV. Personnel working on fire protection systems must be certified per UFC 3-601-02 and shall be licensed in the state of Mississippi, as applicable. Fire Protection services shall be managed by a qualified individual who is NICET level III certified in fire alarm or NICET level III certified in special hazards systems. Personnel working on fire protection systems shall be certified in accordance with the requirements below: Fire Alarm Systems: ? Fire Alarm: NICET Level II certification in Fire Alarm Systems. ? Detection and releasing systems for Special Hazard Systems such as those found in aircraft hangars and computer server rooms: NICET Level II certification in Special Hazard Systems Water Based Suppression Systems: ? Wet Pipe and Dry Pipe Sprinklers: NICET Level II certification in Inspection and Testing of Water Based Systems. ? Pre-Action, Deluge, Foam and Antifreeze Systems: NICET Level III certification in Inspection and Testing of Water Based Systems. Special Hazard Systems: ? Clean Agent, CO2 and Combination Detection/Releasing Systems: NICET Level II certification in Special Hazard Systems. Pre-Engineered Kitchen Fire Extinguishing Systems: ? NICET Level II certification in Special Hazards Suppression Systems or certified by ICC/NAFED in Pre-Engineered Kitchen Fire Extinguishing Systems. The service technician shall have the applicable manufacturer�s design, installation, and maintenance manual and service bulletins. Less qualified personnel may assist NICET Levels II and III certified personnel in the execution of inspection, testing, maintenance and repair task. At no time shall less qualified personnel be allowed to execute inspection, testing, maintenance and repair task without a qualified NICET Level II or III. The Contractor shall also perform maintenance on NAS Meridian Water Plant SCADA system to ensure proper operation, to minimize breakdowns, and to maximize useful life.The Contractor shall conduct annual testing, calibration and adjustment of the system form the control point to the terminations at the monitoring devices, individual well houses, chemical mixers or injectors, valves and motor controllers. The performance of this contract requires maintenance, monitoring, programming, and integration services on specific proprietary control systems, Life Safety systems, and Industrial Control Systems (ICS). These include, but are not limited to, Johnson Controls, Simplex, Monaco, and Honeywell systems, as well as SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) water control systems. Interested sources must demonstrate existing technical competency, direct access to necessary proprietary software/firmware/tools, and current Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) authorization, certifications, or formal partnership agreements required to service, modify, and maintain these proprietary systems without voiding warranties or compromising system integrity. Respondents should be prepared to provide: (1) Proof of active OEM authorization/certification or licensed integrator status for the listed proprietary systems; (2) Evidence of personnel holding relevant manufacturer credentials/certifications (e.g., NICET II+ for fire alarm systems, certified ICS/PLC programmers for plant control); and (3) A brief summary of past performance involving identical or similar proprietary systems within an operational environment.

description: September 10, 2026 It was brought to the government's attention that previous solicitation amendments cannot be accessed. They now have been activated and are accessible. August 19 2026: Please see amendment 0002 attached and an updated Section L. August 11 2026: 1. Please see amendment 0001 attached and an updated Section L dated 5 August 2026. 2. The government is accepting RFIs until 21 August at 3PM EDT. If you have already sent your RFIs to the POCs you do not have to resubmit them. 4 August 2026: Please see the attached RFP (FA8137-26-R-0040) and all attachments. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- THIS POSTING WILL SATISFY THE REQUIREMENT OF RFO 5.101, Presolicitation Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) for General Construction Services will accomplish a broad range of sustainment, maintenance, repair, alteration/renovation, and minor construction projects affecting real property facilities at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. title: Notice Of Intent to Sole Source - Thermo Fisher Scientific Asheville LLC - Centrifuge Calibration
description: The purpose of this acquisition is to have Health Effects Laboratory Division (HELD) centrifuges undergo preventative maintenance and calibration. Regular calibration of centrifuges is essential because it ensures that rotational speed, temperature control (when applicable), and timing functions remain accurate, which directly affects the reliability and reproducibility of experimental results. The vendor shall perform visual and functional checks for rotor condition, imbalance indicators, lid locks, refrigeration performance (where applicable), and overall mechanical integrity. Key parameters will be calibrated according to International Standard Organization (ISO) 17025 standards.

It is not a request for quotes nor does it obligate the government in any way. The Government will not reimburse the respondents for any costs associated with the information submitted in response to this request. Additionally, this RFI notice does not guarantee that the government will issue a request for quotes or award a contract for supplies or services. The National Weather Service (NWS), Ocean Prediction Center (OPC), U.S. National Ice Center (USNIC) has a need for georeferenced GeoTIFFs of global coverage in accessible electronic format 24/7/365 and with the capability of near-real-time latency. SAR imagery�s benefits remain helpful to the persistence of USNIC�s operational programs of earth surface observation in the poor weather or illumination conditions of the polar latitudes. Near-real-time latency is considered to be the capability of delivering images deemed to be time critical to USNIC no more than approximately four (4) hours from time of satellite acquisition. title: Collaborative Testing Services (CTS) Proficiency Testing Supplies
description: This notice announces the intent by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) Fort Detrick, Maryland, 21702, to award a sole source Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract to Collaborative Testing Services (CTS) under the statutory authority 12.102(a). The contract is for the purchase of Scheduled proficiency tests shipped at specified dates (vendor dependent) to include testing materials (bloodstains, dried body fluid stains, dried saliva samples) for the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES), Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory (AFDIL). Collaborative Testing Services, LLC (CTS) is the only responsible source capable of providing the highly specialized proficiency testing supplies and services required to maintain the accreditation and operational integrity of the Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory (AFMES/AFDIL). While four proficiency testing providers are recognized by laboratory accrediting bodies�Collaborative Testing Services, Bode Cellmark Forensics, College of American Pathologists (CAP), and Serological Research Institute (SERI)�comprehensive market research and technical evaluation confirm that only CTS satisfies the agency�s minimum operational, throughput, and scientific requirements. The remaining three providers present critical technical deficiencies that make them unsuitable for AFDIL�s casework requirements: Bode Cellmark Forensics offers infrequent testing schedules that cannot support AFDIL�s staffing capacity or rolling test intervals; SERI imposes compressed completion windows that are incompatible with the extended processing times required by AFDIL�s advanced testing technologies; and CAP utilizes a manual, scan-based submission process that introduces an unacceptable risk of data transcription errors. In contrast, CTS uniquely provides the validated test substrates, electronic reporting infrastructure, and staggered distribution schedules necessary to efficiently test personnel on a continuous basis without disrupting critical forensic operations. Procuring these tests from any other source would jeopardize compliance with time-sensitive accreditation standards, compromise the validity of future casework, and introduce substantial risks to the laboratory's mission. CTS is the sole provider that meets all required sample matrices, capacity requirements, and distribution intervals. Delivery Date: 01 November 2026 The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 334516 and the size standard is 1,250 Employees. This is a notice of intent to issue a contract on a sole source basis. This notice of intent is NOT a request for quotations (RFQ). Any other firms desiring consideration must fully identify their interest in and capability to provide these services to the individual listed below. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written responses are received by the expiration date listed in this notice, which reflects at least fifteen (15) days after the publication of this notice, the award will be issued as sole source. All questions and responses concerning this notice shall be emailed to Mr. Christopher L. Cook at christopher.l.cook68.civ@health.mil.

Constructs a low-rise open air standing seam-metal roofed canopy on a reinforced shallow foundation with wide-flange beams and columns and continuous footings for a Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile Processing Facility (Motor Transfer Facility). Functions include receiving and shipping missile motors, components and Active Inert Missiles (AIMS) which require superflat floors for air pallet operations. The roof structure will include sloped, uninsulated metal roof panels on steel joists. Any resultant contract will be firm-fixed price. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction with the annual size standard of $45.0 million.
