Under the FAR guidelines, the prime contractor must have the capability to perform at least 20 percent of the contract work with its own employees. The period of performance is 527 calendar days. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. title: P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES AT KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA
description: This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) Southeast is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project involves constructing railroad trackage to connect and facilitate the transfer from commercial rail to the on-base processing facility at Cape Canaveral. Constructs a low-rise open air standing seam-metal roofed canopy on a reinforced shallow foundation with wide-flange beams and columns and continuous footings for a Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile Processing Facility (Motor Transfer Facility). Functions include receiving and shipping missile motors, components and Active Inert Missiles (AIMS) which require superflat floors for air pallet operations. The roof structure will include sloped, uninsulated metal roof panels on steel joists. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 237990. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $25,000,000 � $100,000,000. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 527 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.504(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. In light of recent court decisions on PLAs, the Government is seeking additional information on the use of PLAs for this project. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. (See question #4) Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Deborah Torrence, deborah.d.torrence2.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00 PM ET on September 25, 2026.

title: Blanket Purchase Agreement - Sample Testing
description: The requirement is for the establishment of single Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for the testing of metal coupons to aid the QA process of the components with which these coupons are associated. The Contractor�s laboratory facility must be validated by the USACE Materials Testing Center (MTC) along with maintain ISO/IEC 17025 certification and remain validated throughout the life of this agreement. Project Background The Contractor shall receive, test mechanical and/or chemical characteristics, and submit reports of coupon materials to aid the QA process of the associated components supplied to the Government via other ongoing contract efforts. The coupons will be shipped directly to the Contractor, many of which will likely come from international locations. The Contractor will not be responsible for shipping or duty costs to receive coupons. The coupon materials that may be tested include but may not be limited to ASTM A743 Grade CA6NM and Grade CF3, ASTM A27 Grade 70-40, ASTM A148 Grade 80-40, ASTM A216 Grade WCC, and ASTM A516 Grade 60. The tests that may be required include chemical analysis according to ASTM A751, carbon combustion according to ASTM E1019-18, tensile tests (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation, and reduction of area) according to ASTM A370, hardness tests according to ASTM A370, and Charpy v-notch impact tests according to ASTM A370. The range of tests completed for a given coupon will depend on the material and component with which it is associated. There may be provisions for optional storage of coupons, both tested and untested. Disposal of excess coupons may be considered at no additional cost to the Government.

description: NHTSA's New Car Assessment Program (NCAP) requires pedestrian protection impact testing on production motor vehicles. The Government intends to make multiple awards and to issue firm-fixed-price task/delivery orders for testing as vehicle models are assigned. valuation: Award will be made on a best-value tradeoff basis considering the following technical factors � (1) Technical Plan, Quality Assurance Management Plan, and Test Procedures; (2) Facilities and Equipment; (3) Organization and Personnel Qualifications; and (4) Past Performance and Prior Experience - and price. The technical factors, combined, are more important than price. Please see the attached for the full solitcitation and all support documents.

title: BEYOND Phase 2
description: Amendment 0001 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to September 25, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0001. __________________________________________________ This is the Screening Information Request (SIR) 697DCK-26-R-00423 for the BEYOND Phase 2 Selection. This procurement is in support of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Office (AUS). The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. To be considered for award of this requirement, the Offeror must have a current/valid registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database website: www.sam.gov. Registration must be active by the offer due date. Proposals must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 3:00 pm ET on September 10, 2026. Please see attached SIR for proposal submission requirements. Questions are to be submitted, in writing, as specified in the SIR. Please reference the SIR number and BEYOND Phase 2 program on all question submissions. All questions must be received no later than 1:00pm ET on September 3, 2026. Questions will be answered in an Amendment to the SIR if deemed necessary and posted to SAM.GOV for all interested parties to consider. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Kristin Frantz, Contracting Officer, at Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov and Jackson LeMay, Contract Specialist, at Jackson.T.Lemay@faa.gov Any proposals received after the closing date and time, will not be considered in accordance with this SIR. This SIR is not to be construed as a contract or a commitment of any kind. The Government will not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation.

title: Multi-Domain Cyber & Intel Operations Center, Lackland Air Force Base, Texas
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, on behalf of the Department of the Air Force (DAF), is issuing this solicitation announcement to identify a Design-Build (DB) team for a new Multi-Domain Cyber & Intel Operations Center (MDCIOC) at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA), Lackland AFB, Texas. The proposed project involves the design and construction of an approximately 600,000-square-foot, multi-story facility to consolidate the 16th Air Force's Information Warfare workforce. The new center will be a state-of-the-art, 24/7 facility designed to the highest security and technical standards, including ICD 705. The project will house over 3,000 personnel and support global cyberspace operations, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). The project delivery model will be a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) executed through an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement. The acquisition will be conducted in two phases: Phase 1: Design and Pre-Construction Services: The selected DB team will collaborate with the Government to advance the design and refine project requirements. Phase 2: Full Design and Construction: Upon successful negotiation of a fair and reasonable price, the OT may be modified to include the final design and construction. The Government will use a two-step, qualifications-based selection process: White Paper Submission & Evaluation. Pitch Meetings (by invitation only). Request for White Papers: Interested parties are invited to submit a White Paper in accordance with this announcement and its attachments. The White Paper is the only submission required at this time and must address all requirements outlined in Attachment 1 of the solicitation to be considered. Submissions should demonstrate the respondent's qualifications, project understanding, and relevant experience. Questions Due Date: All questions must be submitted via the ProjNet Bidder Inquiry System by September 18, 2026, in accordance with the instructions in the solicitation. White Paper Due Date: White Papers must be submitted via email to the Solicitation POCs no later than 2:00 PM CT on September 25, 2026. Email Subject Line: "White Paper for Multi Domain Cyber & Intel Operations Center" Please refer to the attached solicitation document and Attachments for complete details on the project scope, submission requirements, and evaluation criteria.

title: Sources Sought - Gainesville IRMS
description: Opportunities Description The Department of Veterans Affairs currently occupies office and related space in a building under a lease in Gainesville, Florida, which will be expiring. The Government will consider alternative space if economically advantageous. In making this determination, the Government will consider, among other things, the availability of alternative space that could satisfy the Government�s requirements, as well as the costs likely to be incurred through relocation, such as physical move costs, replication of tenant improvements and telecommunications infrastructure, and non-productive agency downtime. The Department of Veterans Affairs desires to lease approximately 10,773 RSF of office space in Gainesville, Florida, for use by VA personnel, furnishings, and equipment for the Gainesville IRMS. Fifteen (15) parking spaces are required. A lease of up to 6 years/2 years firm will be considered. The space must be ready for occupancy no later than October 1, 2027. The lease space must be fully serviced to include all utilities, landscaping, trash removal, and janitorial services. Lease space within the following boundaries will be considered: NORTH: Intersection SW Archer Rd & SW 34th Street SOUTH: US Hwy 441 EAST: Intersection SW 34th Street & SW Williston Road WEST: Interstate-75 A market survey of offered properties may be conducted by VA staff. Building name and address, along with the location of the available parking spaces The expected rental rate per rentable square foot Total number of spaces available Availability date of the spaces Ownership details and authorization from the owner, if applicable List of services provided (utilities, janitorial services, pest control, security, etc.) This requirement is currently housed in an existing leased space.
